headline: Approved contracts for new Assistant Principal, Preschool Coordinator, Interim Principal, and renewed senior staff contracts; awarded food service and facilities bids.
summary: The School Committee held an executive session on personnel matters, then in open session approved several contract and bid items, including new administrators, a food service contract with Chartwells, and mechanical and snow removal service contracts. In the afternoon summer workshop, the Committee discussed collective bargaining, an equity audit, FY 2027-2028 budget planning, self-evaluation and goal setting, and committee norms, with no votes taken on those items.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including executive and open session minutes, purchases over $10,350, and homeschool requests for SY 2026-2027, 5-0.
Accepted the Settlement of Appeal regarding NEASK Non-Renewals as presented in Executive Session, 5-0.
Accepted the Terms of Contract Negotiation for the Assistant Principal, South Kingstown High School, 5-0.
Accepted the Terms of Contract Negotiation for the (0.5) Preschool Coordinator, 5-0.
Accepted the Terms of Contract Negotiation for the Interim Principal, Broad Rock Middle School, 5-0.
Approved Contract Renewal for the Assistant Superintendent, Director of Student Services, Human Resources Coordinator, and Executive Assistant to the Superintendent and School Committee, 5-0.
Approved the SY 2026-2027 Food Service Contract with Chartwells, 5-0.
Accepted the Mechanical Service Contracts 2026-2028 (Bid #SK0028FAC) as presented, 5-0.
Accepted the Bid Award for RFP #2473, Snow Removal Services 2026-2028, as presented, 5-0.

7.  Open Annual Summer Workshop/Roll Call 
  
A. Roll Call 
 Ms. Vetter called the Annual Summer Workshop to order at 10:00 AM and led the roll call. 
 
     Members present:  Carol Vetter, James Restivo, Michelle Brousseau, Paula Whitford, Kate Macinanti (arrived at 10:14 AM) 
     Stewart Lander 
     Members absent: None 
     Others present: Michael Podraza, Superintendent; Daniel Seger, Assistant Superintendent; Patricia Proctor, Chief Financial  
     Officer; Joseph Adams, Director of Facilities and Operations; Charlene Longolucco, Human Resources Coordinator 
 
8.  School Committee Annual Summer Workshop  
 
A. Discussion: School Committee Professional Development - Collective Bargaining - Presentation by William E. O'Gara, 
Esquire 
 
Mr. Podraza introduced William O'Gara, Esquire, who discussed the challenges of negotiating collective bargaining agreements in        
Rhode Island, emphasizing the impact of declining student enrollment on school budgets. Attorney O'Gara highlighted the significant 
increase in medical insurance costs, noting a $13 million-dollar expenditure for all benefits. He explained the concept of "evergreen" 
contracts, which prevent unilateral changes, and stressed the need for detailed homework (looking at Union contracts of other 
districts) and determining realistic goals. The discussion also covered the importance of maintaining goodwill with unions and the 
potential for incentives to encourage senior staff to retire.  
 
B. Discussion: Equity Audit - Latest Data Points and Upcoming Administration Actions 
 
Mr. Podraza discussed the progress and future plans regarding the equity audit, emphasizing the review and revisions of 
handbooks, implementation of alternative consequences, and professional development for Administrators and Deans.  He shared 
how current work is being directly aligned to the findings of the equity audit, with a focus on addressing identified gaps rather than 
simply tracking trends. He reviewed ongoing revisions to handbooks and procedures, the implementation of alternative 
consequences and restorative practices, and the use of the new SurveyWorks portal to monitor indicators such as school belonging, 
student–teacher relationships, and student perceptions of absenteeism. He noted an 8% increase in students’ recognition that 
chronic absence harms academic performance. Mr. Podraza outlined upcoming professional development with the Liber Institute, 
where all building administrators will be trained in the Power Framework, to include empathy interviews, and student focus groups to 
better understand student experiences.  This training will aid in the design of school-specific interventions, including Administrators 
shadowing students in other buildings. The discussion connected this work to the equity audit’s call for professional development for 
all adults, noting a district-wide information professional development day on the September 9 Primary Election Day for all staff.  
During this day, staff will use a rubric to assess their practices along a continuum from trauma- inducing to trauma-informed and 
trauma-invested, with the expectation that harmful practices identified through this process will be addressed through the educator 
evaluation system. Committee members emphasized the need for this work to result in consistent classroom-level implementation, 
clearer communication to families about how these efforts will change school culture and safety for all student groups, and the use of 
Superintendent and Administrative goals, informed by SurveyWorks and other data, to ensure accountability and ongoing 
improvement.
4  
 
C. Lunch Break 
 
Lunch Break is taken at this time (12:15 PM to 12:45 PM). 
 
D. Discussion: FY 2027-2028 Budget Planning and Preparation 
 
Mr. Podraza reviewed major fiscal drivers, including the pending statewide CTE tuition recalculation and Warwick litigation; declining 
enrollment and rising coastal property values that shift the funding formula and increase the local share; as well as significant costs 
pressures in salaries and benefits, particularly double-digit health insurance increases.  He noted that FY 2027 includes 
approximately $1 million from fund balance and that the district likely ended in a surplus; though final figures depend on closing 
transportation and payroll encumbrances and receiving delayed Medicaid reimbursement.  Discussion ensured regarding prioritizing 
remaining RIDE-approved capital projects (with a 35% reimbursement) before the current plan’s December 2027 deadline. 
Discussion further ensued regarding the need to clarify the handling of state housing aid reimbursements in the Town-held school 
capital reserve fund.  Committee members agreed that the recent budget cycle with the Town Council was problematic and 
committed to starting the FY 2028 budget process earlier.  The Committee would like to host School Committee led budget work 
sessions beginning in September, holding multiple joint meetings with the Town Council before formal budget season, using current-
year enrollment and financial data to inform projections, and strengthening transparency and community engagement throughout the 
process. 
 
E. Discussion/Action: School Committee Self-Evaluation and Goal Setting 
 
Mr. Restivo shared the recent results of the School Committee Self-Evaluation.  This self-evaluation was conducted using an 
anonymous questionnaire completed by five of its members.  Members generally rated the Committee positively on governance, 
policy work, professionalism, and internal climate, noting strong collaboration, respect, trust in administration for day-to-day 
operations, and effective policy development and updating. They identified areas for improvement in (1) community engagement and 
feedback (few community members regularly attend meetings; shared interest in reviving community workshops and better 
outreach), (2) use of data in decision-making (more regular use of achievement and performance data, clearer link to strategic plan 
monitoring, and more data-rich presentations), and (3) goal follow-through (Committee-set goals were not consistently kept “front 
and center” over the past year).  
 
The Committee then reviewed last year’s goals and agreed they had not been kept sufficiently visible or used to guide work, then set 
updated goals for the coming year. They agreed to: (1) improve meaningful community engagement by holding additional work 
sessions, possibly five over the academic year, and exploring ways for the public to comment on specific agenda items (2) redesign 
and start the FY 2028 budget process earlier, including a review of the last three years’ budget timelines and scheduling multiple 
School Committee–hosted joint meetings with the Town Council beginning in September; (3) remove barriers to learning 
opportunities for both students and staff, with specific mention of improving access to CTE programs and professional development; 
and (4) strengthen the Committee’s use of data in decision making, including at least two substantial data-focused presentations tied 
to student outcomes, program effectiveness, and strategic plan monitoring. Further discussion regarding making goals more 
“SMART” (specific and measurable) by attaching concrete indicators (e.g., number of workshops or Council meetings) and having 
goals regularly referenced at meetings so they remain central to the Committee’s work. 
 
No vote was taken on this item. 
 
F. Discussion/Action: Update of School Committee Norms 
 
The Committee reviewed its current meeting norms, with several members noting that the existing list had largely been created 
externally, was not deeply discussed when adopted, and is only partially aligned with how the current Committee actually operates. 
Members agreed that some concepts remain important—such as students first, coming to the meeting prepared, trusting the process, 
using data to inform decisions, and confronting difficult issues rather than avoiding them.  Members questioned the need for others 
(e.g., separate “confidentiality” and “respect” norms that are already covered by ethics and law). Discussion ensued as to how norms 
could be used more actively to support community engagement (structuring agendas to allow public comment on business items) 
and how they could tie directly to their new goals. The Committee agreed to keep this item as a work in progress, with this 
conversation being a short draft set for now. The Committee would like administration to research example norms from other districts 
and will revisit and finalize norms after the upcoming election when the full seven-member Committee is seated, so that all members 
can participate in crafting and owning the final set. 
 
No vote was taken on this item. 
 
9. Adjournment  
A. Adjourn
